quote.text: Les feuilles tombent, la figue sèche, remplace la figue fraîche, le raisin sec la grappe mûre, voilà selon toi des paroles de mauvaise augure ! Mais il n’y a là que la transformation d’états antérieurs en d’autres ; il n’y a pas de destruction, mais un aménagement et une disposition bien réglée. L’émigration n’est qu’un petit changement. La mort en est un plus grand, mais il ne va pas de l’être actuel au non-être, mais au non-être de l’être actuel. Alors ne serais-je plus ? Tu ne seras pas ce que tu es mais autre chose dont le monde aura alors besoin.
quote.author: Epictetus
quote.aiInsight:
• Parenthood
    • Just as nature transforms—a fig changes from fresh to dried and leaves fall—parenthood is a series of transformations. Embrace each stage of your child's growth as a reordering of potential and possibility.
    • Understand that the evolving nature of your relationship is not a loss but an opportunity to nurture new virtues. By accepting change, you pave the way for your child to blossom into their destined role.
  • Leadership
    • In leadership, the inevitable changes within a team or organization are akin to the transition of seasons. View each shift not as an end but as a necessary reorganization that prepares the ground for future excellence.
    • Recognize that your role is to guide these transformations with clarity and purpose. Like the natural cycle of becoming and reshaping, an effective leader fosters growth, adapting strategies as circumstances evolve.
  • Product Management
    • Much like nature's cycles illustrated in Epictetus’ words, product management thrives on the constant evolution of ideas. Each iteration, whether refreshing or retiring a feature, is part of a deliberate process of refining what the market needs.
    • Approach product transformation with a mindset that sees change as an inevitable reordering of value. By embracing evolution, you can design products that continue to meet the shifting demands of a dynamic world.
